parsed.explanation: Combined regime is restrictive at every level. Nationally, passport sex-marker restrictions are in force after a November 2025 Supreme Court ruling, and entry cables direct refusal on any document discrepancy, with a possible lifetime fraud bar. National immigration custody has documented abuse of transgender detainees, and national corrections policy adopted from 2026 is documented as harmful. The state adds birth-sex facility bans in government buildings, a 2026 marker-invalidation law, a documented trespass-based arrest of a trans visitor-equivalent, a refusal-to-depart trespass offence, no state gender-identity hate-crime coverage, a religious-refusal statute, and a minor name-change bar. Offsets are real but limited: national same-sex marriage recognition, four municipal ordinances, national hate-crime and employment protections, and a near-baseline killing rate (6.6 vs 6.0 per 100k). Overall, Elevated to High Risk.

entry_documents.exposure: Passports cannot be marked other than M or F per birth-sex documents; new applications and markers not matching birth sex are refused. Entry cables direct refusal for any discrepancy or reasonable doubt, and a possible permanent fraud ineligibility finding. Passports have been confiscated or blocked, leaving some travellers stranded.
entry_documents.protection: Existing X passports remain valid until expiry. Litigation is pending. No documented operative protection for visitors at entry.
entry_documents.interaction: Document mismatch at entry leads to refusal or referral, and a refusal can escalate to fraud allegation and lifetime ineligibility. Discrepancy is the trigger.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Documented national immigration custody abuse of transgender men, including forced labour, beatings, solitary confinement and severe sexual abuse. A state trespass offence allows arrest and 24-hour holding in a men's ward for a trans woman using a women's restroom.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Trespass requires willful entry plus refusal to depart when asked, not arrest on entry. Civil-rights litigation exists.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Facility use in a state building can move from employee request to trespass arrest, then to a sex-based holding ward. Document doubt can feed into national detention.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: State bans on facility use by gender identity in government buildings, including schools and colleges, and in some private settings across the national map. The state defines sex by birth in statute and enacted bans in 2024 and 2025. National corrections conversion-style policy applies to trans inmates.
federal_state_facilities.protection: Facility bans in the state are not documented as applied to adult visitors. Four municipal ordinances protect against discrimination in public accommodation.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: National and state rules layer. Municipal protections do not override the state facility ban, which applies to government buildings.

care_services.exposure: State bans on gender-affirming care under 18. The state's largest public hospital closed its adolescent clinic. National subpoenas of hospital records for patients under 19. Proposed national rules to bar public insurance reimbursement for under-18 care. Medication withheld in national custody.
care_services.protection: A single LGBTQ-specialising clinic operates in one city. No documented protection of visitor care access.
care_services.interaction: Care-seeking minors can be exposed to records subpoenas. Medical records are a discovery channel at the national level.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: National executive framing groups radically pro-transgender politics with violent secular extremism. A cash reward system targets leadership of such groups. The state court calls a trans minor a 'minor female'. The national strategy prioritises neutralising such groups.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: The national strategy disclaims targeting people who only disagree. No documented enforcement against visitors on these grounds.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Official threat framing and state court language add to document and facility exposure, but this is secondary for a visitor without advocacy activity.

minors_guardians.exposure: A minor visitor faces state school bathroom and sports rules, a state minor name-change denial, and an under-18 care ban. A dress-code threat was documented for a trans girl at school. A parent or guardian may face national threats of prosecution for facilitating social transition.
minors_guardians.protection: Visitors may avoid school settings. A chancellor may grant name change where clearly in the child's best interest.
minors_guardians.interaction: Travelling with a minor exposes the pair to document checks, and a minor's medical need can become a records and prosecution issue.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: One documented bias-motivated killing of a trans woman in 2017, with no later instance documented. The killing rate of 6.6 per 100k per year is near the general homicide rate of 6.0, so it is background-level rather than trans-specific campaign. Restroom arrest is documented.
street_violence_police_response.protection: National bias-killing prosecution produced a 49-year sentence. The state has no gender-identity bias-crime statute. Pride events occurred in one university town.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Police response to a trans victim is not documented. Street violence is near baseline, but state-level hostility reduces reporting and recourse.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Passport and facility litigation is unresolved. The state name-change ruling accounts conflict and are unresolved. Adult enforcement of facility bans against visitors is not sourced. The dual birth-certificate listing and the March 2026 licence law's treatment of visitors are unsourced.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Same-sex marriage is recognised nationally. National hate-crime and employment protections exist. Municipal ordinances in four cities. Public opinion is trending more supportive among younger residents.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Recourse is slow and uncertain. Unknowns are open questions and weigh lightly, but the documented exposures remain the main driver.

anchor_checks.comparison: Similar. Both use universal entry exclusion and a document-driven refusal with no effective appeal. This case has no register-based exclusion and no documented administrative removal of a visitor, but it adds a permanent fraud-bar possibility and national custody abuse, so it sits in the same band.

Similar. Both document birth-sex housing or facility rules with harmful custody outcomes and a cross-dressing-type arrest. This case has no documented criminal statute for presentation at state level, no documented sweeps, and no custody birth-sex housing at state level, so it sits slightly higher.

Lower. The 0.45-D case has registration of visitors and shared database exposure. This case has documented entry refusal, custody abuse and birth-sex facility rules, which are heavier tier-1 exposures, so it sits below.

parsed.synthesis: The traveller's first exposure is the passport: a sex-marker mismatch triggers refusal and possibly a lifetime fraud finding, with no working remedy in force. A mismatch or facility dispute can move into trespass arrest and a men's-ward holding, and national immigration custody has documented abuse of trans detainees. State facility bans and a state defined-sex statute extend the exposure to government buildings, while care and name-change restrictions bear on minors. Mitigations are real but mostly resident-facing or indirect: national marriage recognition, national hate-crime and employment protections, municipal ordinances, and a killing rate at near-baseline background. The documented tier-1 exposures outweigh these, placing the case in the high-to-elevated risk band.
